title: CTIS Report
description: CTEM Interchange Schema (CTIS) 2.0: one producer's observations of assets, findings, dependencies, relationships and endpoints. A document carries natural keys (canonical forms) and the producer's own references, never a receiver's database keys. Normative semantics: docs/spec.md. Media type application/vnd.ctis+json; version=2.0, file suffix .ctis.json.

version.description: CTIS specification version as MAJOR.MINOR. Receivers decode a document of their own or an older minor strictly, ignore unknown members and map unknown enum values to their fallback in a document of a newer minor, and reject another major (spec section Versioning). 1.x documents are rejected.

$schema.description: Schema URL, normally https://schemas.openctem.io/ctis/2.0/report.json. An identifier: receivers never fetch it.

rules.description: Rules and checks the findings name by rule_ref, described once

relationships.description: Typed relationships between two assets of this report, named by their ids

endpoints.description: Methods and paths web origins serve, as a tool saw them; parameters are named, never valued

Extensions.description: Namespaced producer data: keys are reverse-DNS namespaces (io.openctem, com.example.scanner), values objects that namespace defines. A receiver validates a namespace it knows and ignores one it does not. At most 32 namespaces and 64 KiB serialized (the size is checked by Validate).

TargetOutcome.description: How one target of the work ended, in the vocabulary of the outcome package: done and unfinished take no class or cause; failed and skipped need a class of their own

target.description: The target as the work was given it (a name, an address, a range, a URL)

Segment.description: This document's place in a result split over count documents that share one metadata.id. index is zero-based.

Relationship.description: A typed edge between two different assets of the report

from_ref.description: The asset the relationship starts from

to_ref.description: The asset the relationship points to

first_seen_at.description: When the producer first observed the edge

last_seen_at.description: When the producer last observed the edge

confidence.description: How sure the producer is of the edge, 0-100

RelationshipType.description: One direction per type, read as from <type> to; no inverse duplicates

ReportMetadata.description: Report metadata. No member carries a tenant identifier: the tenant comes from the credential.

id.description: Producer-generated UUIDv7 that identifies this document: the idempotency key. A retry re-sends the same id; receivers deduplicate on (credential, id). Every segment of a split result shares it. Never a receiver's key.

generated_at.description: When the producer generated the document (RFC 3339 with offset)

channel.description: How the data reached the document: scanner, collector, integration, manual. A separate axis from the detection technique.

source_refs.description: The producer's own references for the work (a job id in its scheduler, a scan id in the source product)

coverage_type.description: Coverage type: full (complete scan), incremental (diff scan), partial (specific directories)

profiles.description: Conformance profiles the producer claims for this document

started_at.description: When the work that produced the report started

ended_at.description: When the work that produced the report ended

targets.description: How each target of the work ended. An item seen earlier on target T is gone only when a coverage_type full report lists T with state done and omits it

BranchInfo.description: Git branch context for CI/CD scans. Used for branch-aware finding lifecycle management.

is_default_branch.description: Whether this is the default branch (main/master). Auto-resolve only applies to default branch scans.

base_branch.description: Base branch for PR/MR scans (e.g., 'main' when scanning a PR targeting main)

pull_request_number.description: PR/MR number if this is a pull request scan

techniques.description: Detection techniques the tool applies (closed set). A finding may override with its own technique.

content.description: Content releases the tool ran with: template and rule packs, vulnerability databases

Properties.description: An opaque bag. Receivers MUST NOT give meaning to its keys; namespaced data goes in extensions.

Technique.description: Detection technique: how a finding was found

SourceRef.description: A producer's own identifier of an item in its own system ({system, id}): a plugin id, a scan id, an issue key. Never a receiver's key; receivers never use it as one.

system.description: The system that issued the id, an open token

DocumentRef.description: A document-local reference (id and *_ref members): links items inside one document and means nothing outside it. At most 255 visible ASCII characters, and never UUID-shaped, so a receiver's database key cannot be passed off as one.

Rule.description: A rule or check described once; findings name it by rule_ref and keep an equal rule_id

id.description: Document-local reference findings name the rule by

rule_id.description: The tool's identifier of the rule

help.description: How to fix what the rule finds (plain text)

help_uri.description: Page that documents the rule (http or https). Receivers never fetch it.

default_severity.description: Severity the tool gives the rule when a finding does not override it

tags.description: The tool's tags for the rule

cwe_ids.description: CWE identifiers the rule checks for

content_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the rule's content as the tool ran it (a template or rule file), lowercase hex

content_path.description: Path of the rule within the tool's content (plain text; receivers never open it)

ToolContent.description: One content release a tool ran with

name.description: Content name, for example a template pack or a vulnerability database

sha256.description: SHA-256 of the release, lowercase hex
